 Could weather have an impact on the 2026 elections?
 BY 
 Spectrum News Weather Staff
 Nationwide 
 PUBLISHED 12:00 PM ET Nov. 02, 2026 
 PUBLISHED 12:00 PM EST Nov. 02, 2026 
 SHARE 
 Election Day falls on the first Tuesday of November. Have you ever wondered why? Election day comes after the fall harvest and before winter’s harshest conditions typically move in.
 Weather traditionally plays at least a marginal role in determining voter turnout.
 Dating back to America’s first elections in the 1700s, weather has played a big role in election turnout. Long trips to polling places are the reason Election Day falls on a Tuesday. While the trips are much shorter in the modern era, some studies show inclement weather can still impact voter turnout. 
 Precipitation and previous elections 
 Studies going back decades suggest that rain and other uncomfortable conditions can make a trip to the polls less appealing. In most studies, though, the drop in turnout is small.
 A 2023 paper, “ When the election rains out and how bad weather excludes marginal voters from turning out ,” reviewed 34 earlier studies on rainfall and voting and added its own analysis. Authors Søren Damsbo-Svendsen and Kasper M. Hansen found that local rainfall lowers the probability of voting. On average, each additional inch of rain cuts turnout by about 1 to 2 percentage points. 
 The study looked at elections around the world, including in North America, Europe and Asia. A widely cited U.S. study found a smaller effect: a little less than a 1 percentage point drop in turnout for each inch of rain, and about half a point for each inch of snow.
 Precipitation isn't everything 
 Precipitation gets the most attention in these studies, but another study of the 2004 election looked at other factors. It found that sunshine and mild temperatures were associated with lower overall turnout. For every 10-degree rise in temperature, the probability of voting dropped by 0.6 percentage points.
 Election Day 2020 pointed the other way. The weather was fairly pleasant, with very little precipitation, and according to the U.S. Census Bureau , the election had the highest voter turnout of the 21st century .
 As with any of this research, correlation doesn’t necessarily equal causation.
 What's the outlook for 2026? 
 While temperatures will be above-average in many spots across the country on Election Day, rain and storms will be possible for many voters as well. The chance for rain and storms extends south from the Upper Midwest to the Southeast. There's also a chance for a few showers in Northern California.
